# Neo.mjs v13.3.0 Release Notes

**Release Type:** *pending: the operator confirms it at the cut.*
**Stability:** *pending: the operator confirms it at the cut.*
**Upgrade Path:** A drop-in replacement for 13.2. Both new grid features are opt-in and the package's entry points are unchanged; see *Upgrading from 13.2* below.

> **Status: iteration 1 of N — a deliberately-early draft.** Its chapters come from the stewards' deposits on [#19712](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19712), checked against their primaries. Screenshots, the release designation, the cut's own receipt and the numbers regenerated at the cut head follow in later iterations.

> **TL;DR:** 13.2 took fourteen weeks and 2,195 pull requests. 13.3 is the first release on the one-to-two-week cadence set after it, so it carries one theme it could finish: the buffered grid meets real content. A grid can now size its rows to their wrapped text, measured by the browser's own layout, while the row you are reading stays still. Its headers can open a menu that filters a column by checked values, with live counts. Beside the theme, the release process changed: a cut now goes through a pull request and `dev`'s required checks like every other change, and every Engine pull request runs the end-to-end tier that hosted CI used to skip.

---

## 📋 13.3 in 2 Minutes

**The one line:** the grid fits its content. Rows grow to their wrapped text, headers filter by value, and the visible rows hold still while the grid measures.

**Three cornerstones**, each finished within 30 hours of its first post:
1. **Content-sized rows** ([#19658](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19658)). `contentSizedRows: true` sizes every row to its tallest wrapped cell, across the start, center and end bodies. A hidden pre-render measures the text, so the heights are the browser's own layout. 17 hours from the Discussion's first post to the epic's close.
2. **Grid header menus** ([#19643](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19643)). `columnMenu: true` gives each column a value picker with search and live counts, opened by right-click, a hover arrow, the keyboard or touch. 29 hours from the Discussion's first post to the last merge.
3. **A cut the maintainers can run** ([#19637](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19637)). `publish.mjs` releases through a pull request, without the ruleset bypass that 13.2.0's cut needed. 15 hours from the ticket to the merge. This release's own cut is planned as its first real run ([#19652](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19652)).

**Beside them:** the Brain-gated end-to-end tier now runs on every Engine pull request, and a red blocks the merge. A full run is 266 tests on ten shards; a pull request outside the tier's impact boundary runs an eight-file smoke set. The burn-in found three engine bugs before the tier blocked anything.

**The scale:** 48 pull requests merged in `neomjs/neo` and 50 issues closed in three and a half days, since 13.2.0 was published on 2026-10-11 at 22:37Z (GitHub search, run 2026-10-15 09:00Z). The *Full Changelog* at the end lists them by area; the counts are regenerated at the cut.

**The short route:** open [`examples/grid/contentSizedRows`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/examples/grid/contentSizedRows/index.html). It shows 10k records whose wrapped text sizes their rows, with a toolbar toggle back to fixed 32px rows as the control. For header menus, set `columnMenu: true` on a grid; no shipped example turns it on yet.

**The limits:** content-sized rows are proven at 10k rows, not 100k. Header menus count local data only. Until 2026-10-25, a failing end-to-end test gets one retry, and the run's receipt names it. Each chapter's *Honest bounds* says more.

**Read for your work:** the two grid chapters if your grids show text or need filtering; the cut and the end-to-end tier if you contribute or release; *Upgrading from 13.2* if you ship the Engine.

## 📏 Content-sized rows: the grid fits its text

A buffered grid keeps a small pool of row elements and moves them over a large store as you scroll. Until 13.3 it did this on one assumption: every row has the same height. Wrapped text was either cut off or given rows tall enough for the longest cell. Variable row heights had been on the grid's backlog since March ([#9495](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/9495)). 13.3 lets a grid drop the assumption:

```javascript
{
    module          : GridContainer,
    contentSizedRows: true,
    store           : MainStore,
    columns         : [
        {dataField: 'title',   locked: 'start', text: 'Title',   width: 160, wrapText: true},
        {dataField: 'summary',                  text: 'Summary', width: 280, wrapText: true},
        {dataField: 'owner',                    text: 'Owner',   width: 110}
    ]
}
```

Each row takes the height of its tallest `wrapText` cell in all three bodies, so locked columns stay aligned with the center. Fixed height stays the default, and a fixed-height grid is unchanged.

### Measured by the browser, not predicted

The first convergent shape on [D#19645](https://github.com/orgs/neomjs/discussions/19645) predicted heights in the App Worker, with a third-party text-layout library among its candidates. About two hours after the Discussion opened, the operator turned it:

> [!NOTE]
> *"not sure if we need pretext, since neo has already pre-rendering tools inside main, and we can easily build more or adjust. we want to avoid using 3rd party libs as much as possible."*
> — Tobi, 2026-10-12 ([the direction, as the Discussion records it](https://github.com/orgs/neomjs/discussions/19645#discussioncomment-18880598))

The engine already measured text by rendering it. `MagicMoveText` briefly renders characters into a hidden measure element, and `DomAccess.getBoundingClientRect` reads a whole array of element ids in one round trip. A probe priced the pass: 300 cells rendered with the grid's cell CSS into a hidden container, one forced layout, every height read. It took 3.6 ms in Chromium 153 and 4 ms in Firefox 155 and WebKit 26.6 (medians of 7 runs), and the worker-to-main round trip stayed under 0.1 ms. The heights are exact by construction: every font, script, zoom level and CSS rule is the browser's own.

### Eight pull requests in seventeen hours

The App Worker keeps one row-geometry model per view, and it drives the scroll offsets, both scroll extents and keyboard navigation ([#19668](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19668)). Cells of `wrapText` columns are measured in place ([#19672](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19672)), and a hidden pre-render measures rows before they mount ([#19688](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19688), by @neo-gpt). When a measured height replaces an estimate, the correction keeps the visible row and the pinning origin still ([#19674](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19674)). `AnimateRows` stands aside in content-sized mode ([#19677](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19677)). The Discussion opened at 10:22Z on 2026-10-12, and the epic closed at 03:16Z the next morning, 16 hours and 54 minutes later.

### Three defects the journey found

**A recycled row took its previous record's height.** On the example's 100k-row draft at 1400×900, jumping to row 99,996 and pressing ArrowDown four times left the last row 100px tall, while its text needed 81px. 100px was the height of the record that had last used that pooled row. The DOM lagged the vdom with no flag set, because a view's update waits for in-flight child updates without marking itself. Before the fix, 18 of 20 headless runs ended with the stale height; after it, none of 20. A cell is now read only once the DOM shows it ([#19692](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19692), [#19695](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19695)).

**macOS fonts hid a 1px defect that Linux CI found.** Every local run passed on macOS. In CI, a test failed: row 4 shrank from 62px to 43px when its column mounted. The hidden measuring cells kept the 1px right border that a region's last column drops (`neo-last-column`). Under Arial metrics, which CI's Linux fallback font shares, that pixel wrapped record 4's details to three lines hidden and two shown. The fix passes `isLastColumn` to the hidden projection, as `Row#createVdom` does, and a unit test compares a hidden cell's classes with its displayed cell's, so the two cannot drift apart again. Swept over five fonts, two runs each, no row changes ([#19704](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19704)).

**A hidden grid kept measuring.** A grid under `display: none` retried its zero-width measurements: 267 batches with the old behaviour. @neo-gpt's fold pauses the work until layout returns, and the counter reads zero ([#19688](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19688#issuecomment-6135355216)).

### The proof

`ContentSizedRowsExample.spec.mjs` turns D#19645's ten required examples into named end-to-end tests, one per example, against the browser's layout: a row needs its tallest text plus the cell's chrome ([#19704](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19704)).

### Honest bounds

- 10k rows, not 100k. Past 2^23 px, Chrome rounds scroll offsets to 2 px, and browsers cap element heights at different limits ([#19658](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19658#issuecomment-6134339160)). Scaled scrolling beyond that is deferred.
- Deferred by the epic: tree stores, images and components in cells, remote data, and uniform or capped N-line modes.
- `AnimateRows`' pre-existing fixed-height breakage stays open as [#6858](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/6858).

## 🔽 Grid header menus: filter a column by its values

An engine user asked for a header menu whose first tool is a value picker with counts. 13.3 ships it, opt-in:

```javascript
{
    module    : GridContainer,
    columnMenu: true,
    columns   : [
        {dataField: 'firstname', text: 'Firstname'},
        {dataField: 'id',        text: 'Id', columnMenu: false}
    ]
}
```

Right-click a header, or use the arrow button that appears on hover or focus, Shift+F10, the ContextMenu key, or touch. One floating picker opens, with literal option search, a count beside every value, and checkboxes that filter at once. The selection belongs to the Store, so two grids on one store, or a header rebuilt later, show the same filter. Sorting, resizing and reordering keep their own paths ([#19711](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19711)).

### Counting without touching the data

Counts read the whole local population and apply every filter except the picker's own, so a value's count is how many rows hold it under the other filters. There is no remove-and-reapply cycle, no hydration and no write to the raw data: on the 100k-record `bigData` store, sampled raw keys and values stay unchanged through open, search and recount ([#19673](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19673), [#19711](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19711)).

### Whose filter is it?

The store looked filters up by property, and the first match won. An [executed discriminator](https://github.com/orgs/neomjs/discussions/19646#discussioncomment-18880470) on D#19646 showed what that would do to a menu: in two creation orders, the picker's filter and an application's own filter on the same field overwrote each other. Ownership moved into `Collection` and `Filter` as a (role, dataField) identity, and the property-only lookup is kept for existing callers.

### Review caught what green tests passed

The host pull request's first review round found two defects its tests had passed. One checkbox toggle on an open menu ran two full count passes, which the PR's own receipt priced at 85–155 ms each at 100k. And numbers sorted as text (`1, 10, 100, 2, 20`), dates by weekday name. Both were fixed before the second round approved ([review](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19711#pullrequestreview-5499524532)). A follow-up gives Date values locale-aware labels, and empty strings, `null` and `undefined` distinct visible ones ([#19724](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19724)).

### Numbers

- 19 native end-to-end cases in four specs, green on the first attempt in hosted CI ([run 38413337763](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/38413337763)).
- The picker admits at most 1,000 unselected matches. On the id column of 100k records, a refine footer asks for a narrower search, and all seven refusal codes render as messages.
- Three pull requests by @neo-gpt, +4,631/−177 lines, 28 hours and 44 minutes from the Discussion's first post to the last merge.

### Honest bounds

- Opt-in by design. A grid without `columnMenu` renders its headers as before, and that is tested.
- The 100k timings are a bounded witness, not a performance promise.
- Deferred: a grid-level search toolbar, exclusion mode, hide, lock and width commands, a column chooser, and remote, partial and tree populations.

## 🚦 A cut the maintainers can run

13.2.0's cut stopped twice on 2026-10-11. `git push origin dev` was refused, because `dev`'s ruleset requires CodeQL and 18 checks on every pushed commit (GH013). After the operator added a bypass, the local pre-push battery stopped the squash onto `main`. The release was finished by hand, and npm had 13.2.0 at 22:37Z. The script dated from 13.1.0 (July 3); the ruleset arrived on July 17 and its required checks on October 10, and no rehearsal had ever pushed ([#19637](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19637)).

After the publish, the operator removed the bypass instead of keeping it, and set the requirement: the AI maintainers must be able to trigger a release. A standing bypass would let anything that authenticates as the bypassing account land on `dev` past CI and CodeQL. So a release now takes the path every change takes ([#19653](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19653)):

1. `publish.mjs prepare` opens the release pull request, and `dev`'s required checks and CodeQL run on it.
2. The operator merges it: the one human step.
3. `publish.mjs finish` squashes the merge onto `main` and creates the GitHub release.

Re-running a command continues a phase that stopped. Two review rounds by @neo-gpt-sophie shaped the rest:
- **An unknown never passes for an absence.** A failed read used to become an empty list, `false` or a clean tree, so a 403 on the rules or a failed `git status` could have shown a green gate. A proven absence (a recognised 404, an empty ref) is now separate from an `ObservationError`, which stops the phase and shows as ❌ under `--rehearse`.
- **A ref is reused only when it belongs to this release.** An open release PR with no local branch read as *waiting*, and a release whose tag commit was unknown read as *released*. A missing identity now refuses.
- **13.2.0 itself is refused.** It was published outside this workflow, so its tag is not a merged release PR's merge commit.

One pull request, +735/−167 lines, with 19 cases in `ReleaseState.spec.mjs`: 14 hours and 45 minutes from the ticket to the merge, 71 minutes from the PR's opening.

### Honest bounds

- So far the path is proven against a scripted command boundary, plus a live `--rehearse` against the real rules and tickets, run as a maintain-role account that cannot bypass. The real-cut criteria wait for 13.3.0's own cut ([#19652](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19652)), and these notes claim the first pull-request-gated cut only after `finish`, npm and the Portal have verified it.
- `finish` pushes the squash with `--no-verify`, on purpose: the squash flattens every reviewed change since the last release into one commit, which the pre-push spec-retirement check fails by construction. A comment beside the push says why.

## 🧪 Every Engine pull request runs the end-to-end tier

Until 13.3, hosted CI deselected every Brain-gated end-to-end spec, the ones that drive the app through the Neural Link: 96 of 145 spec files never ran there ([D#19599](https://github.com/orgs/neomjs/discussions/19599)). A dock regression from [#19559](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19559) sat red but unseen on `dev` for about 14 hours, until a bisect found it.

**Burn-in before blocking.** A failing check blocks a pull request's formal review even when it is not required, because `validateMergeReady` refuses any failure. So the tier first ran on `dev` pushes, where nothing read it, and measured its hosted time ([#19667](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19667)). It gained ten shards and a receipt that declares its hosted gaps ([#19676](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19676)), a virtual screen large enough for the multi-window journeys ([#19683](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19683)), and one retry per failing test until 2026-10-25, with every retried test named ([#19682](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19682)). Then it was promoted: every Engine pull request runs the full tier or a smoke set, chosen by the shared classifier, and a red blocks ([#19705](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19705)). From the burn-in ticket to the promotion took one day.

**The burn-in found engine bugs, not only flaky tests.** Each was fixed for its class:
- A component inserted into another window kept a settled `mountedPromise`, and `updateVdom()` looped on it. It was the burn-in's most frequent red. While a component is unmounted, the getter now hands out a pending promise ([#19689](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19689)).
- `Overflow.project()` read a tab header destroyed mid-projection as live, and logged its own teardown as a defect ([#19701](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19701)).
- Undoing a popup's native close let main's late return projection take the pane back, and the pane ended up in neither window. A Group projection now stands down once a newer commit has adopted its participant's next document ([#19703](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19703)).

**A bridge with an end date.** A retry runs in a fresh worker, so it heals a cross-file leak every time. Every receipt therefore names each retried test, and the bridge expires on 2026-10-25 without anyone editing it. Each quarantine names an owner and an exit, and goes stale after seven days.

**The numbers:** the full tier is 95 files and 266 tests on ten shards, and its slowest test step took 3m53s against a five-minute ceiling. The first `dev` run after the promotion passed all 266, with one healed by the retry ([run 38403855169](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/38403855169)).

### 🕵️ War Story: the test that drove someone else's app

**Symptom.** While the header menu's host leaf was being built, a fresh test page called `connectToApp('Neo.examples.grid.bigData')` and bound an older session of the same app, one that had `columnMenu: true` set. The test's writes went into that other page's grid ([#19713](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19713)).

**Investigation.** `connectToApp` asked the page for its own App Worker id through `page.waitForFunction(async () => …)`. A probe on the pinned Playwright 1.63.0, against a page that sets a value after 1,500 ms:

| Predicate | Result |
|---|---|
| `async () => window.id ?? null` | `null` after 9 ms |
| `() => window.id ?? null` | `"ready"` after 1,492 ms |

**Culprit.** Playwright treats the async predicate's Promise as truthy, so the wait resolved on its first read and never polled. During bootstrap that read is `null`, and the fixture fell back to binding by app name, which resolves to the oldest session with that name. All 139 `connectToApp` calls pass a name. The async predicate had been in the fixture since 2026-06-11 ([#12904](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/12904)).

**Fix the class.** `connectToApp` no longer binds by name ([#19715](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19715)). Given a name, it binds the page's own App Worker, polling for its id for up to 30 seconds, and fails if none arrives. Given an App Worker id, it binds that id. With the old read restored as a mutation, the new test that connects an older same-name session first goes red: the fixture binds the older one.

## 🧰 Also in 13.3

- **Animated sorting moves each card once.** An animated component list moved its retained cards twice before settling on a new sort order; now they move directly to the latest order ([#19717](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19717), [#19738](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19738)).
- **A Canvas renderer that fails to load is not reported ready.** `SharedCanvas` now reads the Canvas worker's module-load result: a refused import settles initialization, emits `canvasLoadFailed` and keeps a mountable shell ([#19732](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19732), [#19734](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19734)).
- **A request to a departing window says so.** An in-flight request rejected because its worker port retired now carries `NEO_DEAD_PORT` and the target window id ([#19728](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19728)).
- **Dock animations land before a resize.** `DockFlip.land()` restores the captured geometry with CSS transitions suppressed, so a native resize reads the landed geometry ([#19708](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19708)).
- **The Workstation film restores its saved two-window arrangement** ([#19569](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19569), [#19731](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19731)). It was one of the two restore defects the roadmap carried; the other, [#16498](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/16498), stays open.
- **The Portal features the Workstation first** in every example mode ([#19641](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19641)). The npm 13.2.0 package still carries the old catalogs, so the site serves the correction from an overlay until 13.3.0 publishes it.
- **Both RealWorld apps boot again.** Their API singletons waited on a static `Base.on('ready')` that no class provides, so every singleton after the first threw. They now share one stored-token promise ([#19700](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19700)).
- **A grid keyboard-navigation failure captures its state** for diagnosis ([#19654](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19654)). The intermittent failure itself stays open as [#19515](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19515).

### 🤝 From the community

@sloemo01, whose component spec for the Portal's CSS 3D cube appeared in 13.2, closed a ticket filed on 2023-02-17 ([#4069](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/4069)): reordering the items of a header toolbar should keep the gaps between them. The base sort zone's `switchItems` already did. [#19710](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19710) pins its gap math for the tab, grid and table headers, including the unequal-size case behind the ticket's 1.5px drift note.

## ⬆️ Upgrading from 13.2

**Nothing to change.** `package.json`'s `main`, `exports`, `bin`, `engines`, `type` and dependencies are unchanged; between `13.2.0` and `d2014f4433` its only change is a devDependency, `neo-agent-skills` 0.1.39 → 0.1.41. Both grid features default off: `contentSizedRows: false` on the grid, and `columnMenu: false` on the grid with a per-column override.

**Public behaviour to check:**

| If your code… | In 13.3 | Do this |
|---|---|---|
| awaits `mountedPromise` on a component that is not mounted | the promise stays pending until the next mount; before, a promise settled by an earlier mount could be returned at once ([#19689](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19689)) | nothing, unless you relied on the early resolve |
| catches the rejection of a remote call whose target window is closing | the error keeps its `PortDisconnectedError` name and message, and adds the code `NEO_DEAD_PORT` and the target window id ([#19728](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19728)) | branch on the code if you need to |
| loads a Canvas renderer through `SharedCanvas` whose import can fail | the host no longer reports ready; it emits `canvasLoadFailed` ([#19734](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19734)) | listen for the event if you need a fallback |
| looks a store's filter up by property while a header menu filters the same field | each writer owns its filter by (role, dataField); the property-only lookup still returns the first match ([#19673](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19673)) | nothing |
